title: Roger Williams
hook: banished from Massachusetts, he founds Rhode Island with freedom of conscience for all

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Mayflower, the Pilgrims and the Puritans: real help and real harm. Your line was freedom for whom?

The court in Massachusetts has decided: the young minister must leave the colony. His crime isn't theft or violence. It's ideas. He's been saying that the government has no business punishing people for how they worship, and that the king's charter can't hand over land that belongs to the Native peoples who live on it. Tradition says he slipped away in winter, before they could ship him back to England, that Native people sheltered him, and that Narragansett leaders let him settle on their land. There he founded a settlement where nobody would be punished for their conscience. He called it Providence.

Roger Williams was a Puritan himself, and an intense one. He wasn't arguing that faith didn't matter. He was arguing that it mattered too much to be forced. A belief pressed on someone at the point of a sword, in his view, isn't faith at all. He leaned on a parable of Jesus. A farmer sows good seed, and an enemy comes by night and sows weeds among the wheat. The servants want to pull the weeds out at once. The farmer says no, in the King James Bible: "lest while ye gather up the tares, ye root up also the wheat with them. Let both grow together until the harvest". For Williams, that settled it. Sorting true believers from false isn't a job for magistrates and courts. It's God's, at the harvest. This freedom came to be called soul liberty: the freedom of each person's conscience before God, which no government should touch. He pictured a hedge or wall between the garden of the church and the wilderness of the world, to protect the garden. And he lived it. His colony became a place where Baptists, Quakers and Jews could worship openly. He disagreed sharply with some of them in public debates, but he didn't drive them out. He learned the Narragansett language, wrote a book about it, and insisted land be bought from its people rather than simply taken. He could be prickly and stubborn. But the idea he was banished for traveled a long way.

Put a belief you think is wrong into one sentence, the way someone who holds it would say it, fairly, with no sneer. Then say quietly: they have the right to believe this; not that they're right, but the choice is theirs. If you pray, rest with let both grow together until the harvest; if you don't, let the other person stand, unharvested, in your mind.
Roger Williams. A Puritan minister banished from Massachusetts, who founded Providence as a place where no one would be punished for their conscience, a freedom that came to be called soul liberty.
Your line: soul liberty. Faith that matters too much to be forced. That's day eight hundred eighty-six.

howItsDone: Baptists and others in America honor Roger Williams as an early champion of religious liberty, and his idea of soul liberty is still taught in churches that hold to freedom of conscience.
